extracted.intended_audience: Army commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), unit public affairs representatives (UPARs), and Army personnel responsible for public information/releases
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedures governing Army public affairs programs, including who may release information, clearance and prepublication requirements, Web and visual media guidance, use of military assets for public events, and rules for handling sensitive categories of information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff relationship and qualified PA management
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs is a command responsibility; PAOs require direct access to the commander and serve on the commander’s personal staff. Qualified PA personnel designated by the Chief, Public Affairs (CPA) must manage and supervise PA offices, units, sections, and functions. Non-PA staff sections or officials will not be assigned primary responsibility for PA missions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PA offices and functions are managed and supervised only by qualified public affairs personnel; PAOs may be assigned coordinating staff authority as appropriate. (para 1-5a)

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs is an inherently governmental function
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulation and promulgation of Army PA policy is an official responsibility and may be performed only by military or civilian officials of the Army and commanders or their designated official spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not delegate official PA policy formulation or spokesperson duties to non-governmental actors. (para 1-5b)

rubrics_metrics.name: PA mission and use of Soldiers as spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: The PA fulfills the Army’s obligation to keep the American people and the Army informed; every member contributes and Soldiers are the most credible and influential spokespersons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage Soldiers to communicate using all communication mediums while adhering to the guidance in this regulation and related doctrine (FM 3–61). (para 1-6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct communications protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of the Chief Public Affairs (OCPA) may communicate directly with HQDA agencies, Army commands, installations, and subordinate elements if attempts to contact the unit’s higher headquarters in a timely manner have failed; commands/installations may also communicate directly with OCPA after reasonable attempts to contact higher headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any bypassed headquarters must be informed of the direct communication as soon as possible by the office initiating it. (para 1-7)

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearance, review, and approval hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: OCPA/CPA manages the review and clearance of information for release outside DOD; PAOs serve as the commander’s designated review and approval authority for the release of official information to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all necessary staff coordination and clearance are completed prior to releasing information outside the Department of the Army; CPA may process policy exception requests and delegate approval authority in writing. (paras 2-1b, 2-2c(3), 2-4m)

rubrics_metrics.name: PA planning, guidance, and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders will develop PA guidance, strategies, plans, and operations and will evaluate the effectiveness of PA projects, plans, and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders are responsible for establishing and assessing PA plans and ensuring PA support resources and programs meet command needs. (para 2-3a(1)-(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of official spokespersons
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders must designate spokespersons to release information pertaining to their command; the PA is an inherently governmental function requiring official spokespersons to be military or DOD/Army civilian employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only designated government officials may act as official spokespersons. (para 2-3a(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of Unit Public Affairs Representative (UPAR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commanders must appoint a unit public affairs representative to any unit that is not supported by a designated public affairs officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UPARs are command-designated Soldiers, typically an officer from the command staff, who coordinate between the unit, the unit commander, and the supporting PAO. (paras 2-3a(5), glossary)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness, maximum disclosure, candor, and safeguarding
rubrics_metrics.description: Local commanders will provide unclassified information about the Army and its activities to the public with maximum disclosure and minimum delay, be candid, and not release information that would adversely affect national security or threaten personal safety or invade privacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release unfavorable news with the same care and speed as favorable news; balance maximum disclosure with protection of classified/safeguarded information. (paras 2-3d(5)-(6), 3-1b)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and correction of erroneous information
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all information provided to internal or external audiences is accurate and take appropriate action to correct erroneous information about the Army that appears in any medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders and PAOs must verify facts prior to release and promptly correct mistakes. (paras 2-3d(7)-(8))

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of promotional or self-serving releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid promotional, self-serving releases and events staged solely for publicity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs support must not be used to confer selective benefit or to promote individuals or organizations in a way inconsistent with law and policy. (para 2-3d(9))

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination for counterintelligence and sensitive topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of information about U.S. Army counterintelligence personnel or activities must be coordinated in advance with the Deputy Chief of Staff, G-2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate releases on counterintelligence and other sensitive subjects with appropriate security and staff offices before public release. (para 5-24; summary)

rubrics_metrics.name: Health information and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases involving personnel under treatment in Army medical facilities must comply with the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 (HIPAA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with medical and legal authorities and follow privacy/health regulations when releasing medical-related information. (para 5-25; summary)

rubrics_metrics.name: Web content management, approval, and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs serve as the command Web content manager; they must review and release official information intended for the public Web and command Web sites, ensure content approval processes (including coordination with OPSEC officers, security managers, and SJAs), execute information-assurance and Web-risk assessments, and conduct quarterly reviews of publicly accessible Web sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate Web content with CIO/G-6 for policy and maintain oversight and control of Army public Web content; adhere to AR 25–1/AR 25–2 policies for posting and new content. (paras 2-4n, 2-4o, 2-4p, 2-4q, 2-4r, 13-14)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication review and clearance of speeches and manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual governed by this regulation who intends to release information must consult with a PAO; material in its intended release form (book manuscript, magazine article, internet posting, etc.) must be submitted in accordance with chapter 6 for prepublication review. Speaking and manuscript clearance guidelines, authorities, and procedures are in chapter 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retired personnel, former employees, and nonactive duty members of the RCs must use the security review process to ensure releases do not compromise national security. (paras 2-5, chapter 6 summary)

rubrics_metrics.name: Official vs. unofficial discussions and background rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between official discussions with the media and unofficial discussions; 'background' remarks may be reported only if attributed to a nonspecific source and must be agreed on in advance; cameras cannot be used in background sessions and records of background briefings are not FOIA-protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agree on attribution rules in advance for background briefings and follow policies for official/unofficial interactions. (paras 5-12, 5-13, glossary 'Background')

rubrics_metrics.name: Media access, accreditation, and facilitating visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies govern facilitating media visits, media accreditation, media day planning, and official media interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the procedures in chapter 5 for accreditation, media day conduct, and facilitating media access consistent with security and safety considerations. (paras 5-9, 5-10, 5-11)

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual information and photography/recording rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual information products (photographs and videos) and photographing/recording personnel, installations, and equipment are subject to specific policy, including restrictions on photographing installations, equipment, and personnel in hostile areas and rules for release of unclassified official visual information to foreign nationals or governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate visual media release with visual information policy, OPSEC, and appropriate approval authorities; consult paras 5-14, 5-33, and 13-4 for details. (paras 5-14, 5-33, 13-4)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Army resources for events and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Army participation in public events may be authorized only if admission, seating, and all accommodations are available to all without regard to sex, race, creed, color, sexual preference, or national origin; Army resources will be used only to support events of common interest and benefit to broadly represented audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commanders must give equal consideration to comparable events and avoid selective benefit; operational constraints may limit response to requests. (paras 3-1c, 3-1d)

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding, cost-sharing, and events qualifying for funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Public affairs funding authority, use of Army funds and resources, events qualifying for funding, and events requiring user charges or payment for services are governed by chapter 4 and definitions (Army share of costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify Army share of costs (continuing government costs that would exist absent participation) and ensure finance guidelines and contracting rules are followed. (chapter 4, definitions)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization and approval for use of military assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of military assets (musical, aerial, ceremonial, troop units, aircraft demonstrations, etc.) for public affairs requires specific authorization; there are policies on authorized and prohibited participation, criteria for aerial demonstrations, and approval/processing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chapter 7 authority and procedures for requesting and approving aerial and other military-asset activities; forward requests per established timelines and approval chains. (chapter 7 summary, paras 7-1 through 7-11)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and electronic media editorial and style guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance covers primary function, editorial contributions, use of color, photographs and videos, civilian enterprise operations, publication names/mastheads, advertising, news and editorial material, style (including capitalization of 'Soldier' and 'Family'), broadcasting, official Web publishing guidance, blogs and unofficial postings, and fund-raising publicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chapter 13 rules on editorial control, permissible content, official Web site publishing, restrictions on unofficial postings, and style conventions when producing publications or electronic content. (chapter 13 summary, paras 13-1 through 13-16)

rubrics_metrics.name: Event approval timelines and routing to OCPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for support to events that could be of national or international interest must be forwarded through command channels to the OCPA not later than 45 days prior to the event or immediately if the event is within 45 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process and forward timely requests for DA or DOD approval via command channels; consult para 2-3d(3). (para 2-3d(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Special handling for casualty, disciplinary, and criminal investigation information
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of information on casualties, disciplinary actions, criminal investigations, courts-martial coverage, and related matters is subject to specific rules and restrictions to protect privacy, due process, and national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult chapter 5 sections (5-16 through 5-29 and related) for procedures and restrictions governing these sensitive releases; coordinate with legal and investigative authorities as required. (chapter 5 summaries)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to ethics rules and use of good taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Strict adherence to this regulation and the ethics rules in Section 2635 Title 5 Code of Federal Regulation (5 CFR 2635) and DOD 5500.7–R, as well as using common sense and good taste, will result in public support and confidence in the Army.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure PA activities comply with ethics rules and avoid actions that could create appearance of impropriety or selective benefit. (para 3-1b)

rubrics_metrics.name: Event classification and approval authority based on media interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Events are classified as international, national, regional, state, or local; the extent of anticipated or actual news media interest and coverage is one criterion to determine the level of approval authority for Army participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat local and regional events aired nationally on TV/radio as national for approval purposes; use event classification to route approval appropriately. (glossary 'Events')

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidental support criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidental support is support that has a minimal impact on planning, scheduling, functioning, or audience draw of a public event; support is incidental if the question 'Will the event proceed undeterred without DOD assets?' can be answered 'yes'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the incidental support definition to determine appropriate level of PA/military support without creating major involvement or selective benefit. (glossary 'Incidental support')

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Information Bureau (JIB) establishment for major incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: A JIB is established at the scene of a nuclear weapon accident or significant incident to coordinate all PA activities; CONUS JIB will include representation from DOD, DOE, FEMA, and other federal/state/local agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In major accidents/incidents, coordinate multi-agency PA responses through a JIB to ensure consistent messaging and public safety information. (glossary 'Joint Information Bureau', chapter 12 references)

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of unclassified official visual information to foreign nationals/governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of unclassified official visual information material to foreign nationals or governments is governed by specific procedures and restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate release of visual media to foreign entities through prescribed channels and obtain necessary approvals. (para 5-14)

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor and third-party release controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of information by manufacturers, research organizations, educational institutions, and other commercial entities holding Army contracts is subject to rules; clearance and release of contractor materials are addressed in appendix F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contractor-originated releases comply with the regulation, clearance requirements, and any contract restrictions. (para 5-48; app F)
